missed_mechanisms.suggested_classification: WIRE. The counter is monotonic and per-peer, but there is no wrap→rekey handling anywhere on this path (grep for `rekey` in crates/client-core/src returns nothing), and IdentitySeam ignores `args.wire_pn` entirely (seam.rs:117-128 stores it into SealedDatagram and never uses it). corrected_classifications.mechanism: Declared delivery deadline (app budget) → deadline/sRTT ratio (2×RTT calibration endpoint)
corrected_classifications.reason: Its only behavioural consumer is gated by RuntimeConfig::fusion_policy, which is None in default() (runtime.rs:202, with the in-code note 'Sevk default'u KAPALI: kalibrasyon opt-in kalır'). With the default, declare_delivery_deadline stores a value that reaches only diag_tightest_deadline_ns (sender.rs:4175) — a diagnostic-only field, which the task's 'wired' definition explicitly excludes. Default OFF, opt-in, wire byte-identical when off: KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL. The app-facing send_with_deadline API itself is fine to ship; the deadline→behaviour mechanism is not v1.

The finding records spec_requires_v1 = 'optional' and notes it 'is not required by any spec for v1; it is product surface area that exists solely for benchmarking'. SHIP requires 'required for v1'. It is default-inert (fires only on an explicit call, runtime.rs:780/1551) and state-preserving, which satisfies KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL's default-OFF requirement.

WIRE requires spec-required + v1-blocker; engine-spec §11.1 statü (line 849) declares the probe/echo subsystem non-blocking and its absence non-authoritative, so it cannot block v1 — and it is not disconnected, it is unconditionally live. It belongs with its default-OFF client half (bootstrap_rtt: false, runtime.rs:196) — but it FAILS the default-OFF requirement: the responder answers any peer with no gate (runtime.rs:2310-2325), no rate limit (normative: kama-noise-wire §2.57 line 311 'rate-limit T_ECHO_MIN/akış'), no authentication under IdentitySeam (seam.rs:131-137), and it allocates a 105 s PeerSlot per new source address (runtime.rs:2079-2100) in violation of 'receiver'da YENİ state açmaz'. Correct disposition: KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL, with the responder gated behind cfg.bootstrap_rtt (or rate-limited) before v1.

corrected_classifications.reason: Reached only through admit_chunk's frag branch (runtime.rs:1709-1738), gated by max_message_bytes = None by default; slot.msgs is 'never touched' when off (the finding's own feature_off_behavior). Same gate as the fragmenter, so it inherits the fragmenter's classification.

Same default-OFF gate; additionally it is asserted by no test anywhere (only destructured at tests/api_surface_v0.rs:214), and it has two unreviewed behaviours: pop_first evicts the LOWEST message_id rather than the oldest (wrong after the u32 message_id wraps at runtime.rs:1220), and the `>` comparison makes the effective cap 65. Not shippable as-is; not a v1 blocker either, since the feature it bounds is off.

Same default-OFF gate (never runs with max_message_bytes = None). It also carries an ordering defect on its own reject path: `if is_final { self.total_len = Some(end); }` (runtime.rs:1619-1621) executes BEFORE the cumulative-buffer check at :1626-1629, so a rejected oversized FINAL still stamps an unsatisfiable total_len on the assembly. Only the ==0 case is asserted (runtime_e2e.rs:588); the hostile path is untested.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: FEC-recovered chunk joins the SAME delivery admission gate (recovery↔reassembly join)
corrected_classifications.reason: Gate is RuntimeConfig::fec, which is None in default() (runtime.rs:199); with FEC off the frames are counted as unknown_frames (runtime.rs:2224-2226) and no reconstruct path runs. The join logic is correct and well-tested, but it is not part of the shipped default configuration, and its architectural type-gate (kama_engine::admit_and_decode / OpenedTransportShard) is bypassed by the runtime, which feeds raw &[u8] into RsSimdCodec.reconstruct (runtime.rs:1887). Classify as KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL until the FEC default flips and the type-gate is restored.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: Initial-flight window (IW) — PreConverge burst clamp correction
corrected_classifications.reason: Default-ON in the product (runtime.rs:195, 2400 B) but it contradicts a NORMATIVE spec line: engine-spec §3.3-A [K-D2] (lines 301-304) requires 'PRE_CONVERGE'de burst tek-birime clamp'lenir' and names DEFAULT_BURST_CAP itself as the hazard. The code is marked KALİBRE EDİLMEMİŞ twice (sender.rs:313, :4200), and the bench CLI default is 0 on both subcommands (main.rs:123, :238), so the shipped default has never been measured against the profile matrix. A default-ON mechanism that violates a frozen invariant and carries zero measurement is a v1 blocker: either amend §3.3-A with the measurement that justifies the window, or restore the clamp. Not SHIP, not KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL (it is not default OFF).

corrected_classifications.mechanism: Establish probe (DR-EST-1) — PreConverge establishment retry via §3.3-B copy
corrected_classifications.reason: Classification upheld — default-ON (sender.rs:1819), wired through Sender::schedule_transmit into the product drive! loop with no product override (all 12 set_establish_probe call sites are in tests/), and it serves the spec-required §3.3-B establishment-continuity function. But it must ship with a recorded deviation, not silently: it is token-EXEMPT (sender.rs:4064-4070 'token-MUAF'), and engine-spec line 333 states without qualification 'pacer'ı baypas eden gönderim yolu YOK (DATA/retransmit/kopya tek token bucket'ı paylaşır)'. This is the same class of unreviewed default-ON spec deviation as the IW; it differs only in that its function is spec-required.
